<p id="mwDg">The <b id="mwDw">S<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwEA">&amp;</span>P/ASX 200</b> (<b id="mwEQ">XJO</b>) index is a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capitalization-weighted_index" title="Capitalization-weighted index" id="mwEg">market-capitalisation weighted</a> and float-adjusted <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stock_market_index" title="Stock market index" id="mwEw">stock market index</a> of stocks listed on the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Securities_Exchange" title="Australian Securities Exchange" id="mwFA">Australian Securities Exchange</a>. The index is maintained by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_&amp;_Poor's" title="Standard &amp; Poor's" class="mw-redirect" id="mwFQ">Standard &amp; Poor's</a> and is considered the benchmark for Australian equity performance. It is based on the 200 largest ASX listed stocks, which together account for about 82% (as of March 2017) of Australia's share market capitalisation.<sup about="#mwt12" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-2"}}'><a href="#cite_note-2" id="mwFg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwFw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwGA">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwGQ">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwGg">The ASX 200 was started on 31 March 2000 with a value of 3133.3,<sup about="#mwt15" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-3" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-3"}}'><a href="#cite_note-3" id="mwGw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwHA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwHQ">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwHg">]</span></span></a></sup> equal to the value of the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Ordinaries" title="All Ordinaries" id="mwHw">All Ordinaries</a> at that date. The ASX 200 reached 6,000 points for the first time on Thursday 15 February 2007.<sup about="#mwt18" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-4" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-4"}}'><a href="#cite_note-4" id="mwIA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwIQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwIg">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwIw">]</span></span></a></sup> On 22 December 2017, the ASX 200 was 6,069.<sup about="#mwt21" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-5" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-5"}}'><a href="#cite_note-5" id="mwJA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwJQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwJg">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwJw">]</span></span></a></sup> The ASX 200 crossed the 7,000 points level for the first time on 16 January 2020.<sup about="#mwt24" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-6" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-6"}}'><a href="#cite_note-6" id="mwKA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwKQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwKg">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwKw">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

about="#mwt27" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-7" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-7"}}'><a typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-8"}}'><a href="#cite_note-8" id="mwOA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwOQ"><span data-mw='{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"Not a typo","href":"./Template:Not_a_typo"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"^AXJO"}},"i":0}}]}'>^AXJO</span></i><sup about="#mwt29" class="mw-ref reference" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-10" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-10"}}'><a href="#cite_note-10" <meta property="mw:PageProp/toc" id="mwTA" data-mw='{"autoGenerated":true}'/></section><section data-mw-section-id="1" id="mwTQ" aria-labelledby="Calculations"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Calculations">Calculations</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=S%26P/ASX_200&amp;action=edit&amp;section=1" title="Edit section: Calculations"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwTg">The ASX 200 is <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capitalization-weighted_index" title="Capitalization-weighted index" id="mwTw">capitalisation-weighted</a>, meaning a company's contribution to the index is relative to its total market value i.e., share price multiplied by the number of tradeable shares. The ASX 200 is also float adjusted, meaning the absolute numerical contribution to the index is relative to the stock's value at the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_float" title="Public float" id="mwUA">float of the stock</a>.<sup about="#mwt36" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-12" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-12"}}'><a href="#cite_note-12" id="mwUQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwUg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwUw">[</span>12<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwVA">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwVQ">Although the calculation starts with a sum of the market capitalisation of the constituent stocks, it is intended to reflect changes in share price, not market capitalisation. Therefore, a <a rel="mw:WikiLink/Interwiki" href="https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/fudge%20factor" title="wiktionary:fudge factor" class="extiw" id="mwVg">fudge factor</a> called the "Divisor" is used to ensure that the index value only changes when stock prices change, not whenever market capitalisation changes. For example, if a company increases its market capitalisation by issuing and selling new shares to raise capital, the Divisor is adjusted so that the ASX 200 index value does not change.</p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="3" id="mwew" aria-labelledby="Eligibility"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Eligibility">Eligibility</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=S%26P/ASX_200&amp;action=edit&amp;section=3" title="Edit section: Eligibility"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwfA">To be eligible for inclusion in the ASX 200 Index:<sup about="#mwt42" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-14" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-14"}}'><a href="#cite_note-14" id="mwfQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwfg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwfw">[</span>14<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwgA">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<ul id="mwgQ"><li id="mwgg"><b id="mwgw">Market capitalisation:</b> A stock's weight in the index is determined by the float-adjusted market capitalisation of the stock. This is a function of current index shares, the latest available stock price and the Investable weight factor (IWF).  The IWF represents the float-adjusted portion of a stock's equity capital. Therefore, any strategic holdings that are classified as either corporate, private or government holdings reduce the IWF which, in turn, results in a reduction in the float-adjusted market capital. Shares owned by founders, directors of the company, trusts, venture capitalists and other companies are also excluded. These are also deemed strategic holders and are considered long-term holders of a stock's equity. Any strategic shareholdings that are greater than 5% of total issued shares are excluded from the relevant float.</li>
<li id="mwhA"><b id="mwhQ">Liquidity:</b> The trading volume in terms of dollar value and the number of transactions must exceed at least 0.025% of the sum of all eligible securities' trading volume. To ensure that no single company dominates trading, they are capped at a maximum of 15% for value, volume and transactions.</li>
<li id="mwhg"><b id="mwhw">Listing:</b> Only stocks listed on the Australian Stock Exchange will be considered for inclusion in any of the S&amp;P/ASX indices.</li></ul>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="4" id="mwiA" aria-labelledby="Constituent_companies"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Constituent_companies">Constituent companies</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=S%26P/ASX_200&amp;action=edit&amp;section=4" title="Edit section: Constituent companies"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwiQ">The number of companies in the index is dynamic and does not always amount to exactly 200. On average, the index is rebalanced every quarter by Standard &amp; Poor's.<sup about="#mwt45" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-15" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-15"}}'><a href="#cite_note-15" id="mwig"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwiw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwjA">[</span>15<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwjQ">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

href="./Category:All_Wikipedia_articles_in_need_of_updating"/></span>
<p id="mwBA">The <b id="mwBQ">WIG20</b> is a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capitalization-weighted_index" title="Capitalization-weighted index" id="mwBg">capitalization-weighted</a> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stock_market_index" title="Stock market index" id="mwBw">stock market index</a> of the twenty largest companies on the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warsaw_Stock_Exchange" title="Warsaw Stock Exchange" id="mwCA">Warsaw Stock Exchange</a>. Established on April 16, 1994. WIG is an acronym for "Warszawski Indeks Giełdowy", which translates to Warsaw Stock Index in Polish. However, so that no sector would dominate the index, the rule was introduced that there can be a maximum of 5 companies per sector. In this way, for example, there are 5 banks in the index. Companies also have different shares in the index, with clear consequences.<sup about="#mwt6" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-1"}}'><a href="#cite_note-1" id="mwCQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCw">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDA">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwDQ">The all-time high of the index is 3,940.53 points, set during the intraday on 29 October 2007.</p>

<p id="mwDg">In 2013, a new stock market index <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WIG30" title="WIG30" id="mwDw">WIG30</a> was created. It lists the 30 major Polish <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_chip_(stock_market)" title="Blue chip (stock market)" id="mwEA">blue chip</a> companies on the WSE Main Market.<sup about="#mwt9" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-2"}}'><a href="#cite_note-2" id="mwEQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwEg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwEw">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwFA">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<meta property="mw:PageProp/toc" id="mwFQ" data-mw='{"autoGenerated":true}'/></section><section data-mw-section-id="1" id="mwFg" aria-labelledby="Annual_Returns"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Annual_Returns">Annual Returns</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=WIG20&amp;action=edit&amp;section=1" title="Edit section: Annual Returns"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>

<section data-mw-section-id="5" id="mwAQ0" aria-labelledby="Index_ETFs"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Index_ETFs">Index ETFs</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=WIG20&amp;action=edit&amp;section=5" title="Edit section: Index ETFs"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwAQ4">Exchange-traded funds that track the index include:</p>

<ul id="mwAQ8"><li id="mwARA">Expat Poland WIG20 UCITS ETF  - a passive index fund traded in euro and listed in Frankfurt on <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xetra_(trading_system)" title="Xetra (trading system)" id="mwARE">Xetra</a> (ticker <a rel="mw:ExtLink nofollow" href="https://live.deutsche-boerse.com/en/etf/expat-poland-wig20-ucits-etf?currency=EUR" class="external text" id="mwARI">PLX</a>, ISIN BGPLWIG04173). The fund acts as a conduit for capital flows between the international financial markets and the Polish capital market.</li></ul>

<ul id="mwARM"><li id="mwARQ">Beta ETF WIG20TR - a passive index fund traded in Polish złoty and listed on the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warsaw_Stock_Exchange" title="Warsaw Stock Exchange" id="mwARU">Warsaw Stock Exchange</a> (ticker ETFBW20TR, ISIN PLBTETF00015).</li>
<li id="mwARY">PZU ETF WIG20 TR + mWIG40 TR - a passive index fund managed by TFI PZU, traded in Polish złoty and listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange (ticker ETFPZUW20M40, ISIN PLPZUTR00013).<sup about="#mwt25" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-6" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-6"}}'><a href="#cite_note-6" id="mwARc"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwARg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwARk">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwARo">]</span></span></a></sup></li></ul>

<p id="mwDA">The <b id="mwDQ">Financial Times Stock Exchange 100 Index</b>, also called the <b id="mwDg">FTSE 100 Index</b>, <b id="mwDw">FTSE 100</b>, <b id="mwEA">FTSE</b> or, informally, the "<b id="mwEQ">Footsie</b>" <span class="rt-commentedText nowrap" about="#mwt10" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwEg" data-mw='{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"IPAc-en","href":"./Template:IPAc-en"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"ˈ"},"2":{"wt":"f"},"3":{"wt":"ʊ"},"4":{"wt":"t"},"5":{"wt":"s"},"6":{"wt":"i"}},"i":0}}]}'><span class="IPA nopopups noexcerpt" lang="en-fonipa"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English" title="Help:IPA/English">/<span style="border-bottom:1px dotted"><span title="/ˈ/: primary stress follows">ˈ</span><span title="'f' in 'find'">f</span><span title="/ʊ/: 'u' in 'push'">ʊ</span><span title="'t' in 'tie'">t</span><span title="'s' in 'sigh'">s</span><span title="/i/: 'y' in 'happy'">i</span></span>/</a></span></span>, is the United Kingdom's best-known <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stock_market_index" title="Stock market index" id="mwEw">stock market index</a> and represents the 100 most <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Market_capitalisation" title="Market capitalisation" class="mw-redirect" id="mwFA">highly capitalised</a> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_chip_(stock_market)" title="Blue chip (stock market)" id="mwFQ">blue chips</a> listed on the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Stock_Exchange" title="London Stock Exchange" id="mwFg">London Stock Exchange</a>.<sup about="#mwt13" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-ukindexseries_1-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"ukindexseries"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-ukindexseries-1"}}'><a href="#cite_note-ukindexseries-1" id="mwFw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwGA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwGQ">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwGg">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<meta property="mw:PageProp/toc" id="mwGw" data-mw='{"autoGenerated":true}'/></section><section data-mw-section-id="1" id="mwHA" aria-labelledby="History"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="History">History</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=FTSE_100_Index&amp;action=edit&amp;section=1" title="Edit section: History"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwHQ">The index started on 3 January 1984,<sup about="#mwt17" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-factsheet_2-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"factsheet"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-factsheet-2"}}'><a href="#cite_note-factsheet-2" id="mwHg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwHw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwIA">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwIQ">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt20" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-overview_3-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"overview"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-overview-3"}}'><a href="#cite_note-overview-3" id="mwIg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwIw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwJA">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwJQ">]</span></span></a></sup> having been constructed by the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Stock_Exchange" title="London Stock Exchange" id="mwJg">London Stock Exchange</a> to better reflect activity on the market. The index would replace the <i id="mwJw"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_Times" title="Financial Times" id="mwKA">Financial Times</a></i><span class="nowrap" style="padding-left:0.1em;" about="#mwt14" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwKQ" data-mw='{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"&apos;","href":"./Template:&apos;"},"params":{},"i":0}}]}'><span typeof="mw:Entity">'</span></span> own <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FT_30" title="FT 30" id="mwKg">FT 30</a> after its public unveiling on 14 February.<sup about="#mwt22" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-4" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-4"}}'><a href="#cite_note-4" id="mwKw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwLA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwLQ">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwLg">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt25" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-5" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-5"}}'><a href="#cite_note-5" id="mwLw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwMA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwMQ">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwMg">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt27" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-6" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-6"}}'><a href="#cite_note-6" id="mwMw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwNA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwNQ">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwNg">]</span></span></a></sup> As late as 10 February, the Stock Exchange referred to the index as 'SE 100', cutting out the <i id="mwNw">Financial Times</i> who had not contributed to its construction. Recognition was ultimately given to the fact that having the FT involved in the official launch possessed value.<sup about="#mwt29" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-7" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-7"}}'><a href="#cite_note-7" id="mwOA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwOQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwOg">[</span>7<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwOw">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwPA">The new index allowed the Stock Exchange's own London Traded Options Market (LTOM) to launch an <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Option_(finance)" title="Option (finance)" id="mwPQ">options contract</a> derived from the FTSE's real-time data in May 1984, while competitors <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_International_Financial_Futures_and_Options_Exchange" title="London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange" id="mwPg">LIFFE</a> were quick to coincide their launch of the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Futures_contract" title="Futures contract" id="mwPw">futures contract</a>.<sup about="#mwt32" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-8" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-8"}}'><a href="#cite_note-8" id="mwQA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwQQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwQg">[</span>8<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwQw">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt34" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-9" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-9"}}'><a href="#cite_note-9" id="mwRA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwRQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwRg">[</span>9<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwRw">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt36" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-10" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-10"}}'><a href="#cite_note-10" id="mwSA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwSQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwSg">[</span>10<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwSw">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwTA">Usage of the index grew, although the tradeable index contracts struggled to gain traction: annual volume on the FTSE futures contract fell short of 89,000 in 1985, pale in comparison to the 15 million lots traded on the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S&amp;P_500" title="S&amp;P 500" id="mwTQ">S&amp;P 500</a> index contract.<sup about="#mwt38" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-11" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-11"}}'><a href="#cite_note-11" id="mwTg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwTw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwUA">[</span>11<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwUQ">]</span></span></a></sup> By 1986, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margaret_Thatcher" title="Margaret Thatcher" id="mwUg">Margaret Thatcher</a>'s sweeping financial deregulation and high profile privatisations of index members <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BT_Group" title="BT Group" id="mwUw">British Telecom</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Gas" title="British Gas" id="mwVA">British Gas</a>, and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Aerospace" title="British Aerospace" id="mwVQ">British Aerospace</a> had culminated in the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Bang_(financial_markets)" title="Big Bang (financial markets)" id="mwVg">Big Bang</a>.<sup about="#mwt41" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FTSE_100_index_12-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"FTSE 100 index"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-FTSE_100_index-12"}}'><a href="#cite_note-FTSE_100_index-12" id="mwVw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwWA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwWQ">[</span>12<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwWg">]</span></span></a></sup> The combination of a new index, major privatisations, LIFFE tradable derivatives, and promotion by the Financial Times led to the FTSE 100 becoming the most widely used indicator of whether the UK stock market was rising or falling.<sup about="#mwt43" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-13" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-13"}}'><a href="#cite_note-13" id="mwWw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwXA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwXQ">[</span>13<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwXg">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwXw">In 1987, privatisations continued with <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Airways" title="British Airways" id="mwYA">British Airways</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Petroleum" title="British Petroleum" class="mw-redirect" id="mwYQ">British Petroleum</a>. The latter concluded on the same day as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Monday_(1987)" title="Black Monday (1987)" id="mwYg">Black Monday</a>, a crash in which the index fell 21.73% in two days; one of those days is still the index's worst single-day return, –12.22%.<sup about="#mwt44" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FTSE_100_index_12-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"FTSE 100 index"}}'><a href="#cite_note-FTSE_100_index-12" id="mwYw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwZA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwZQ">[</span>12<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwZg">]</span></span></a></sup> While the index was in freefall trading volume of the futures contract hit a record high of 9,111 contracts in a single day. By comparison the volume in the week preceding the crash averaged 2,400 contracts per day.<sup about="#mwt46" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-14" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-14"}}'><a href="#cite_note-14" id="mwZw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwaA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwaQ">[</span>14<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwag">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwaw">By the spring of 1992 LTOM was sold to LIFFE for a nominal sum, consolidating derivatives of the FTSE 100 index into one exchange.<sup about="#mwt48" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-15" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-15"}}'><a href="#cite_note-15" id="mwbA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwbQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwbg">[</span>15<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwbw">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt50" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-16" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-16"}}'><a href="#cite_note-16" id="mwcA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwcQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwcg">[</span>16<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwcw">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt53" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-17" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-17"}}'><a href="#cite_note-17" id="mwdA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwdQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwdg">[</span>17<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwdw">]</span></span></a></sup> Trading of these instruments remained solely in the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institutional_investor" title="Institutional investor" id="mweA">institutional</a> domain since the significant investment required to deliver <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_trading" title="Electronic trading" id="mweQ">electronic trading</a> limited retail access at the time.<sup about="#mwt55" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-18" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-18"}}'><a href="#cite_note-18" id="mweg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwew"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwfA">[</span>18<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwfQ">]</span></span></a></sup> Nonetheless annual volumes for 1992 in FTSE futures and options contracts hit a new high of 2.6 million and 2.2 million respectively.<sup about="#mwt57" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-19" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-19"}}'><a href="#cite_note-19" id="mwfg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwfw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwgA">[</span>19<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwgQ">]</span></span></a></sup> In the autumn the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_England" title="Bank of England" id="mwgg">Bank of England</a> directed by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HM_Treasury" title="HM Treasury" id="mwgw">HM Treasury</a> under <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Major" title="John Major" id="mwhA">John Major</a>'s government failed to prop up <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pound_sterling" title="Pound sterling" id="mwhQ">sterling</a> to maintain the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Exchange_Rate_Mechanism" title="European Exchange Rate Mechanism" id="mwhg">European Exchange Rate Mechanism</a>. A swift <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devaluation" title="Devaluation" id="mwhw">devaluation</a> of sterling on <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Wednesday" title="Black Wednesday" id="mwiA">Black Wednesday</a> and exit from the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Exchange_Rate_Mechanism" title="European Exchange Rate Mechanism" id="mwiQ">ERM</a> benefitted the globally trading FTSE index constituents enormously as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exports" title="Exports" class="mw-redirect" id="mwig">exports</a> became cheaper overnight.<sup about="#mwt59" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-20" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-20"}}'><a href="#cite_note-20" id="mwiw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwjA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwjQ">[</span>20<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwjg">]</span></span></a></sup> Closing on the 15 September 1992 at 2,370.0 the index would almost triple by the end of the decade hitting a high of 6,930.2 on 30 December 1999.<sup about="#mwt62" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-21" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-21"}}'><a href="#cite_note-21" id="mwjw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwkA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwkQ">[</span>21<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwkg">]</span></span></a></sup></p>   

<p id="mwkw">In 2024, there were the most delistings from the London market since the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_financial_crisis" title="2008 financial crisis" id="mwlA">2008 financial crisis</a>, with companies citing higher valuations and cheaper costs available by switching to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Stock_Exchange" title="New York Stock Exchange" id="mwlQ">NYSE</a>. Among them <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashtead_Group" title="Ashtead Group" class="mw-redirect" id="mwlg">Ashtead Group</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CRH_plc" title="CRH plc" id="mwlw">CRH</a>, and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flutter_Entertainment" title="Flutter Entertainment" id="mwmA">Flutter</a> represented almost £120 billion in FTSE 100 <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Market_capitalisation" title="Market capitalisation" class="mw-redirect" id="mwmQ">market capitalisation</a>. Takeovers from <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Private_equity" title="Private equity" id="mwmg">private equity</a> further reduced the available pool of companies that could be drawn on to populate the index, with <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hargreaves_Lansdown" title="Hargreaves Lansdown" id="mwmw">Hargreaves Lansdown</a> also set to delist. Across the entire exchange there were five delistings for every new issue, with speculation at the close of the year around the future of index stalwarts <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_American_Tobacco" title="British American Tobacco" id="mwnA">British American Tobacco</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_Tinto_(corporation)" title="Rio Tinto (corporation)" id="mwnQ">Rio Tinto</a>, and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shell_plc" title="Shell plc" id="mwng">Shell</a>.<sup about="#mwt65" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-exodus_22-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"exodus"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-exodus-22"}}'><a href="#cite_note-exodus-22" id="mwnw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwoA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwoQ">[</span>22<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwog">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="2" id="mwow" aria-labelledby="Description"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Description">Description</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=FTSE_100_Index&amp;action=edit&amp;section=2" title="Edit section: Description"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwpA">The <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stock_market_index" title="Stock market index" id="mwpQ">index</a> has trading symbol UKX<sup about="#mwt66" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-ukindexseries_1-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"ukindexseries"}}'><a href="#cite_note-ukindexseries-1" id="mwpg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwpw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwqA">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwqQ">]</span></span></a></sup> and is maintained by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FTSE_Russell" title="FTSE Russell" id="mwqg">FTSE Russell</a>, a wholly owned <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subsidiary" title="Subsidiary" id="mwqw">subsidiary</a> of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Stock_Exchange_Group" title="London Stock Exchange Group" id="mwrA">London Stock Exchange Group</a>, which originated as a joint venture between the <i id="mwrQ"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_Times" title="Financial Times" id="mwrg">Financial Times</a></i> and the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Stock_Exchange" title="London Stock Exchange" id="mwrw">London Stock Exchange</a>. It is calculated in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real-time_computing" title="Real-time computing" id="mwsA">real time</a> and published every second when the market is open.<sup about="#mwt67" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-factsheet_2-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"factsheet"}}'><a href="#cite_note-factsheet-2" id="mwsQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwsg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwsw">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwtA">]</span></span></a></sup></p><p id="mwtQ">

The FTSE 100 broadly consists of the largest 100 qualifying UK companies by full market value.<sup about="#mwt69" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-23" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-23"}}'><a href="#cite_note-23" id="mwtg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwtw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwuA">[</span>23<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwuQ">]</span></span></a></sup> The total market value of a company is calculated by multiplying the share price of the company by the total number of shares they have issued.<sup about="#mwt72" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-24" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-24"}}'><a href="#cite_note-24" id="mwug"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwuw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwvA">[</span>24<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwvQ">]</span></span></a></sup> The index therefore only reacts to a change in the market value of the companies excluding any dividend income an investor may otherwise reinvest. In order to view the effect of both market value performance and income relative to the FTSE 100 Index alone the FTSE 100 Total Return Index is used. Over the last four decades the total return index has doubled almost five times whilst the index has doubled slightly more than three times respectively.<sup about="#mwt75" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-25" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-25"}}'><a href="#cite_note-25" id="mwvg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwvw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwwA">[</span>25<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwwQ">]</span></span></a></sup></p><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwwg"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:FTSE_100_TR_Index_Line_Chart.png" class="mw-file-description" id="mwww"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:FTSE_100_TR_Index_Line_Chart.png" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/50/FTSE_100_TR_Index_Line_Chart.png/250px-FTSE_100_TR_Index_Line_Chart.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" data-file-width="1654" data-file-height="990" data-file-type="bitmap" height="150" width="250" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/50/FTSE_100_TR_Index_Line_Chart.png/500px-FTSE_100_TR_Index_Line_Chart.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x" class="mw-file-element" id="mwxA"/></a><figcaption id="mwxQ">Total return index from 1986 thru 2026</figcaption></figure><p id="mwxg"> Further, many of these are internationally focused companies: therefore the index's movements are a fairly weak indicator of how the UK economy is faring and are significantly affected by the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exchange_rate" title="Exchange rate" id="mwxw">exchange rates</a> of the pound sterling.<sup about="#mwt78" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-26" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-26"}}'><a href="#cite_note-26" id="mwyA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwyQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwyg">[</span>26<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwyw">]</span></span></a></sup> A better indication of the UK economy is the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FTSE_250_Index" title="FTSE 250 Index" id="mwzA">FTSE 250 Index</a>, as it contains a smaller proportion of international companies.<sup about="#mwt81" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-27" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-27"}}'><a href="#cite_note-27" id="mwzQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwzg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwzw">[</span>27<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw0A">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mw0Q">Even though the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FTSE_All-Share_Index" title="FTSE All-Share Index" id="mw0g">FTSE All-Share Index</a> is more comprehensive, the FTSE<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mw0w"> </span>100 is by far the most widely used UK stock market indicator. Other related indices are the FTSE 250 Index (which includes the next largest 250 companies after the FTSE<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mw1A"> </span>100), the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FTSE_350_Index" title="FTSE 350 Index" id="mw1Q">FTSE 350 Index</a> (which is the aggregation of the FTSE<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mw1g"> </span>100 and 250), <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FTSE_SmallCap_Index" title="FTSE SmallCap Index" id="mw1w">FTSE SmallCap Index</a> and the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FTSE_Fledgling_Index" title="FTSE Fledgling Index" id="mw2A">FTSE Fledgling Index</a>. The FTSE All-Share aggregates the FTSE<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mw2Q"> </span>100, FTSE<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mw2g"> </span>250 and FTSE<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mw2w"> </span>SmallCap.<sup about="#mwt82" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-ukindexseries_1-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"ukindexseries"}}'><a href="#cite_note-ukindexseries-1" id="mw3A"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw3Q"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw3g">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw3w">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mw4A">The index consists of 18 <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Industry_Classification_Benchmark" title="Industry Classification Benchmark" id="mw4Q">ICB</a> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business_sector" title="Business sector" id="mw4g">Supersectors</a>, four of which had a market capitalisation exceeding £250 billion <span about="#mwt83" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mw4w" data-mw='{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"As of","href":"./Template:As_of"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"2026"},"2":{"wt":"June"},"3":{"wt":"30"},"lc":{"wt":"y"}},"i":0}}]}'>as of 30</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt83"> </span><span about="#mwt83">June</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt83"> </span><span about="#mwt83">2026</span><sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;" about="#mwt83"><a rel="mw:ExtLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=FTSE_100_Index&amp;action=edit" class="external text" data-mw-original-href="//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=FTSE_100_Index&amp;action=edit"><span typeof="mw:Entity">[</span>update<span typeof="mw:Entity">]</span></a></sup><span typeof="mw:Nowiki" about="#mwt83"></span><link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:Articles_containing_potentially_dated_statements_from_June_2026" about="#mwt83"/><link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:All_articles_containing_potentially_dated_statements" about="#mwt83" id="mw5A"/>. These are <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banking_in_the_United_Kingdom" title="Banking in the United Kingdom" id="mw5Q">Banks</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pharmaceutical_industry_in_the_United_Kingdom" title="Pharmaceutical industry in the United Kingdom" id="mw5g">Health Care</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aerospace_industry_in_the_United_Kingdom" title="Aerospace industry in the United Kingdom" id="mw5w">Industrial Goods and Services</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oil_and_gas_industry_in_the_United_Kingdom" title="Oil and gas industry in the United Kingdom" id="mw6A">Energy</a>, which together account for approximately 53% of the index's capitalisation.<sup about="#mwt84" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-constituents_28-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"constituents"}}'><a href="#cite_note-constituents-28" id="mw6Q"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw6g"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw6w">[</span>28<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw7A">]</span></span></a></sup> On the same date, there were two companies with a market cap exceeding £200 billion: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AstraZeneca" title="AstraZeneca" id="mw7Q">AstraZeneca</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HSBC" title="HSBC" id="mw7g">HSBC</a>, which together accounted for approximately 18% of the market cap.<sup about="#mwt87" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-constituents_28-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"constituents"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-constituents-28"}}'><a href="#cite_note-constituents-28" id="mw7w"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw8A"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw8Q">[</span>28<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw8g">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mw-A">Each calendar quarter, the FTSE's constituents are reviewed and some companies exit or enter the index, resulting in irregular <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volume_(finance)" title="Volume (finance)" id="mw-Q">trading volume</a> and price changes as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Market_participant" title="Market participant" id="mw-g">market participants</a> rebalance their <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portfolio_(finance)" title="Portfolio (finance)" id="mw-w">portfolios</a>.<sup about="#mwt92" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-overview_3-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"overview"}}'><a href="#cite_note-overview-3" id="mw_A"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw_Q"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw_g">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw_w">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<section data-mw-section-id="3" id="mwAQA" aria-labelledby="Weighting"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Weighting">Weighting</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=FTSE_100_Index&amp;action=edit&amp;section=3" title="Edit section: Weighting"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwAQE">In the FTSE indices, share prices are weighted by free-float capitalisation, so that the larger companies, with more of their stock "floating", make more of a difference to the index than smaller companies. The basic formula for these indices is:<sup about="#mwt95" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-calc_29-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"calc"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-calc-29"}}'><a href="#cite_note-calc-29" id="mwAQI"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAQM"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAQQ">[</span>29<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAQU">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwARQ">The free float factor represents the percentage of all issued shares that are readily available for trading, rounded up to the nearest multiple of 5%. The free-float capitalisation of a company is its <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Market_capitalisation" title="Market capitalisation" class="mw-redirect" id="mwARU">market capitalisation</a> multiplied by its free float adjustment factor. It therefore does not include restricted stocks, such as those held by company insiders.<sup about="#mwt106" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-calc_29-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"calc"}}'><a href="#cite_note-calc-29" id="mwARY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwARc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwARg">[</span>29<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwARk">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwAR4">However, as with any price index the FTSE 100 Index is always changing, whether by corporate action or constituent change. In order to maintain a true reflection of market price movements the <span class="mwe-math-element mwe-math-element-inline" typeof="mw:Extension/math" about="#mwt109" id="mwAR8" data-mw='{"name":"math","attrs":{},"body":{"extsrc":"index~divisor"}}'><span class="mwe-math-mathml-inline mwe-math-mathml-a11y" style="display: none;"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" alttext="{\displaystyle index~divisor}">

<p id="mwASA"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FTSE_Russell" title="FTSE Russell" id="mwASE">FTSE Russell</a> employs the index formula developed by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermann_Paasche" title="Hermann Paasche" id="mwASI">Hermann Paasche</a> for adjusting the <span class="mwe-math-element mwe-math-element-inline" typeof="mw:Extension/math" about="#mwt110" id="mwASM" data-mw='{"name":"math","attrs":{},"body":{"extsrc":"index~divisor"}}'><span class="mwe-math-mathml-inline mwe-math-mathml-a11y" style="display: none;"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" alttext="{\displaystyle index~divisor}">

</section><section data-mw-section-id="4" id="mwAV4" aria-labelledby="Futures_contracts"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Futures_contracts">Futures contracts</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=FTSE_100_Index&amp;action=edit&amp;section=4" title="Edit section: Futures contracts"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwAV8">The benchmark FTSE 100 futures contracts are traded on the ICE Futures Europe (ICEU) exchange, formerly the London International Financial Futures Exchange (<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_International_Financial_Futures_and_Options_Exchange" title="London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange" id="mwAWA">LIFFE</a>). The value of each contract is 10 GBP × index points and is specified as:<sup about="#mwt145" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-liffe_30-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"liffe"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-liffe-30"}}'><a href="#cite_note-liffe-30" id="mwAWE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAWI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAWM">[</span>30<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAWQ">]</span></span></a></sup></p>
<table class="wikitable" id="mwAWU">
<caption id="mwAWY">FTSE 100 (Z) contract specifications</caption>
<tbody id="mwAWc"><tr id="mwAWg">
<th id="mwAWk">Contract size</th>

<tr id="mwAWs">

<td id="mwAW0">ICEU</td></tr>

<p id="mwAYM">On the last trading day of each quarterly futures contract, the settlement price is determined using an intraday auction of all FTSE 100 stocks on the London Stock Exchange, starting at 10:15.<sup about="#mwt146" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-liffe_30-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"liffe"}}'><a href="#cite_note-liffe-30" id="mwAYQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAYU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAYY">[</span>30<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAYc">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwAZg">The index began on 3 January 1984 at the base level of 1,000.<sup about="#mwt149" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-31" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-31"}}'><a href="#cite_note-31" id="mwAZk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAZo"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAZs">[</span>31<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAZw">]</span></span></a></sup> The highest closing value of 10,910.55 was reached on 27 February 2026 and the highest intraday value of 10,989.45 was reached on 31 July 2026.<sup about="#mwt152" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-32" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-32"}}'><a href="#cite_note-32" id="mwAZ0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAZ4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAZ8">[</span>32<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAaA">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<li><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zeneca" title="Zeneca">Zeneca</a> (merged with Astra to form <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AstraZeneca" title="AstraZeneca">AstraZeneca</a>)<sup about="#mwt1024" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-236" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-236"}}'><a href="#cite_note-236" id="mwCEk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCEo"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCEs">[</span>236<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCEw">]</span></span></a></sup></li></ul></div>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="9" id="mwCFA" aria-labelledby="FT_30"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="FT_30">FT 30</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=FTSE_100_Index&amp;action=edit&amp;section=9" title="Edit section: FT 30"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt1028" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwCFE" data-mw='{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"main","href":"./Template:Main"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"FT 30"}},"i":0}}]}'><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1368532237" about="#mwt1029" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw='{"name":"templatestyles","attrs":{"src":"Module:Hatnote/styles.css"},"body":{"extsrc":""}}'/></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt1028" id="mwCFI">Main article: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FT_30" title="FT 30">FT 30</a></div>
<p id="mwCFM">The oldest continuous index in the UK is the FT<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwCFQ"> </span>30, also known as the Financial Times Index or the FT Ordinary Index<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwCFU"> </span>(FTOI).<sup about="#mwt1031" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-237" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-237"}}'><a href="#cite_note-237" id="mwCFY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCFc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCFg">[</span>237<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCFk">]</span></span></a></sup> It was established in 1935 and nowadays is largely obsolete due to its redundancy. It is similar to the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dow_Jones_Industrial_Average" title="Dow Jones Industrial Average" id="mwCFo">Dow Jones Industrial Average</a>, and companies listed are from the industrial and commercial sectors. Financial sector companies and government stocks are excluded.</p>

<p id="mwCFs">Of the original constituents,<sup about="#mwt1034" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-238" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-238"}}'><a href="#cite_note-238" id="mwCFw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCF0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCF4">[</span>238<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCF8">]</span></span></a></sup> three are currently in the FTSE<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwCGA"> </span>100: Tate &amp; Lyle, Imperial Tobacco and Rolls-Royce, although Rolls-Royce has not been continuously listed and Imperial Tobacco was a subsidiary of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanson_plc" title="Hanson plc" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCGE">Hanson</a> for a number of years, and is now renamed as Imperial Brands. Only one of the original FT 30 companies is still in that index:<sup about="#mwt1035" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-239" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-239"}}'><a href="#cite_note-239" id="mwCGI"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCGM"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCGQ">[</span>239<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCGU">]</span></span></a></sup> Tate &amp; Lyle (membership is not strictly based on market capitalisation, so this does not mean they are necessarily among the top thirty companies in the FTSE<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwCGY"> </span>100). The best performer from the original lineup has been Imperial Tobacco.<sup about="#mwt1037" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-240" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-240"}}'><a href="#cite_note-240" id="mwCGc"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCGg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCGk">[</span>240<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCGo">]</span></span></a></sup></p>
